sentences.text: Protosuchus had short jaws that broadened at the skull base to provide a large attachment surface for jaw muscles. Its dentition resembled modern crocodiles, with lower jaw teeth fitting into notches on the upper jaw.
This quadrupedal reptile walked on columnar legs where the rear limbs were longer than the front ones.
The animal was about 80 centimeters in length.
The genus Protosuchus was described by Brown in 1934.
There are 16 recorded fossil occurrences of Protosuchus in the Paleobiology Database.
However, the genus has been synonymized with Archaeosuchus, Baroqueosuchus, and Lesothosuchus.
Other estimates suggest the animal existed from the Rhaetian to the Sinemurian, between 205.7 and 192.9 million years ago.
Researchers interpreting the holotype of Erythrochampsa longipes suggest it may belong to or be a relative of Protosuchus.
